land.text: Zimengchuan 'in present-day Chifeng, Inner Mongolia' (Yuwen page), the capital; the page's infobox region 'ranged from the central part of the present day Liaoning province and eastward' is not drawn, and the Conquest page puts the battle in Liaoning; a 150 km disc round Chifeng

successors.note: 'Murong Huang annexed the Yuwen domain, seized its livestock and treasures, and moved the population to Changli' (Conquest page); more than 5,000 tribes relocated. 'In 344 (or 345), the Former Yan crushed the Yuwen's power base and forced Yidougui to flee, ending their independence.'

ledger.note: 260: the Yuwen under Mohuai. The page lists Yuwen Mohuai 260-293 as the first ruler of a 'pre-state clan of Xianbei ethnicity of Xiongnu origin' that 'was from Liaodong, the region beyond the northern border', with its capital at Zimengchuan. Confidence 1: no sentence dates a founding; the year is the ruler table's.
302: Yuwen Mogui claims the chanyu title. 'During the reign of Yuwen Mogui in 302, he claimed the title of chanyu and boasted a powerful army'; he attacked the Murong and 'was repelled'.

region.text: Zimengchuan 'in present-day Chifeng, Inner Mongolia' (Yuwen page), the capital; the page's infobox region 'ranged from the central part of the present day Liaoning province and eastward' is not drawn, and the Conquest page puts the battle in Liaoning; a 150 km disc round Chifeng

ledger.note: 344: Former Yan destroys the Yuwen. 'In February or March 344 (345 according to the Book of Wei), Murong Huang was finally ready to conquer the Yuwen' (Conquest page); Yan chased the fleeing Yuwen to Zimengchuan, relocated more than 5,000 tribes to Changli, and Yidougui fled to the northern desert. The page gives no day.

wars.name: Yuwen-Murong wars
wars.outcome: Mogui's 302 attack on the Murong was repelled; Xiduguan allied with Cui Bi to attack them in 319; Murong Huang fought the Yuwen 'in 320 and 325' (Murong Hui page); Yidougui backed Murong Ren in the 333 civil war and fought Huang after 336; in 338 the Yuwen took the surrender of Huang's half-brother Murong Han.
wars.note: No page opened gives a result or a place for the 319-325 fights. Murong Han went back to Huang in 340 and led the 344 vanguard.

wars.note: Murong Jun, Murong Ke and Murong Ba commanded divisions; the page gives no day for the battle. 344 or 345 (Book of Wei).

certainty.note: A tribal polity known by its capital and a one-line regional description; no frontier on any page.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; slug yuwen-xianbei, as ea-03-b suggested (the former-yan note: 'Yuwen, Buyeo (jk-02 or ea-03-x)'). The page calls the Yuwen a 'pre-state' clan; the 260 start is the first reign in the ruler table (confidence 1) and the shape a disc round Chifeng. Disagreements: 344 (Conquest page, February or March) against 345 (Book of Wei, Yuwen page infobox 'until its destruction in 345'); the infobox 'central Liaoning and eastward' against the Chifeng capital. The former-yan dossier carries no 344 gain from the Yuwen: it should add one (counterpart yuwen-xianbei) and the Buyeo conquest of 346 stays with the jk-02 group's buyeo dossier. Later Yuwen (Yuwen Tai, Northern Zhou) is the northern-zhou dossier's. Wars with the Murong before 338 have no pages beyond one-line mentions.
